message.content: In lions, the presence of a mane is a classic example of a dominant genetic trait. The allele that codes for a mane is dominant over the allele that results in a maneless phenotype. This means that a lion only needs one copy of the mane allele (heterozygous or homozygous) to develop a full mane, whereas a lion that inherits two copies of the recessive allele will be born without a mane.
